name: POST /api/leadflow/offers/:id/approve - the multi-party route
description:
Records sign-off against a draft version (92ce5959-0e5c-4ce8-be7a-02cc870b2120#AC2). EACH PARTY IS STORED SEPARATELY with who recorded it and when - leadership, legal and finance. A single "approved" boolean lets one person tick a box on everybody's behalf, which is exactly the shortcut the multi-party route exists to prevent, and afterwards nobody can say who actually read the terms.

awaiting[] NAMES WHO IS STILL OUTSTANDING, because "not yet approved" is not an instruction anybody can act on and "legal has not signed" is.

RE-RECORDING A PARTY REPLACES THAT PARTY'S ENTRY rather than appending a second, so the approvals array stays a statement of the current position instead of a log that has to be interpreted.

AN ACTIVATED VERSION CANNOT BE RE-APPROVED IN PLACE. Editing the approval state of terms a buyer has already been shown would make the record disagree with what was signed; a change means a new version.

QA: depends on the draft created by POST /api/leadflow/offers, whose id is read from the cache. All three parties are recorded in one call so the chain can proceed to activation - sign-off frequently arrives as three separate emails that a route administrator records together, and refusing them is how the route gets bypassed rather than followed.

testCases.name: All three parties sign off and the version becomes activatable
NEGATIVE: a party outside the approval route
NEGATIVE: no version with that id
NEGATIVE: no Authorization header at all
NEGATIVE: a bearer token that does not verify

errorCases.message: party must be one of leadership, legal, finance
errorCases.when: no party is named, or a named party is outside the approval route.

errorCases.message: No unactivated offer version with that id - an active version cannot be re-approved in place
errorCases.when: the id does not exist, or the version is already active. Editing the approval state of terms a buyer has been shown would make the record disagree with what was signed.

errorCases.message: Authorization header with a bearer token is required
errorCases.when: the Authorization header is absent, empty, or uses a scheme other than Bearer.

errorCases.message: Session token is invalid or expired
errorCases.when: a Bearer token was presented but does not verify.
